title: Introduction to BM25
text: BM25 is a bag-of-words ranking function that scores documents by term frequency and inverse document frequency with document length normalization.

title: Dense vector retrieval
text: Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents into embeddings and ranks candidates by cosine similarity in vector space.

title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
text: RRF combines several ranked lists by summing the reciprocal of each item's rank, which avoids the score normalization problem.

title: Inverted index basics
text: An inverted index maps each term to the list of documents that contain it, enabling fast keyword lookup at query time.

title: Cross-encoder reranking
text: A cross-encoder scores a query and a document jointly and is used to rerank a shortlist of candidates for higher precision.

title: TF-IDF weighting
text: TF-IDF weights each term by how often it appears in a document against how rare it is across the whole corpus.

title: Approximate nearest neighbor search
text: ANN indexes such as HNSW make vector similarity search fast enough to scale to millions of embeddings.

title: Tokenization and analyzers
text: Analyzers split text into tokens, lowercase them, and drop stop words before the terms are indexed.

title: Evaluating retrieval with nDCG
text: Normalized discounted cumulative gain measures ranking quality by rewarding relevant documents that appear near the top.

title: Hybrid search
text: Hybrid search blends lexical BM25 scores with dense vector similarity to capture both exact terms and semantic meaning.

title: Query expansion
text: Query expansion adds synonyms and related terms to a query in order to improve recall of relevant documents.

title: Vector databases
text: A vector database stores embeddings and supports similarity search together with metadata filtering.

title: Stop words
text: Stop words are very common words like the and is that are often removed because they carry little discriminating meaning.

title: Learning to rank
text: Learning to rank trains a model on labeled query document pairs to order search results by relevance.

title: Chunking documents for RAG
text: Chunking splits long documents into smaller passages so that retrieval returns focused and relevant context to the model.

title: Caching search results
text: Caching frequent queries reduces latency and backend load by serving precomputed results.
